title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Alyssa Chen
release_notes: Consolidated GitHub Actions workflows for lint/test/release; reduced redundant matrix runs; improved build cache usage and parallelism heuristics; bumped actions and standardized Node version to 20 where safe.
description: Context and motivation: Over time the repo accumulated many overlapping CI workflows: separate lint/test workflows per-language, duplicated release automation flows, and ad-hoc cache keys. This caused CI flakiness, long queue times, and increased GH Actions minutes. This PR consolidates lint/test/release concerns into a small set of well-documented workflows, improves cache key hygiene, and introduces a lightweight parallelism heuristic to avoid saturating runners. Goals: 1) Reduce unnecessary matrix permutations for cross-repo changes; 2) Standardize Node runtime to Node 20 where supported across SDKs; 3) Improve cache hit rate and reduce wall-clock time for CI; 4) Keep release automation behavior identical (no user-facing changes). Changes summary (commits): - 1st commit: add unified workflows/.github/workflows/ci-unified.yml consolidating lint and test jobs with conditional paths and lightweight matrix pruning. - 2nd commit: replace multiple release workflow files with workflows/release-pipeline.yml; preserve tagging and changelog steps but consolidate upload artifacts. - 3rd commit: implement cache key normalization helper and shared actions composite (tools/actions/cache-normalize). - 4th commit: bump commonly used GH Actions (actions/checkout, setup-node) and standardize node-version: 20.x in most TS/JS steps. - 5th commit: small fixes from review: reduce job concurrency, add explicit restore-keys for cache, and opt-in for legacy Node 16 flows for older packages. Files changed (high level): - .github/workflows/ci-unified.yml (new) - .github/workflows/release-pipeline.yml (new) - .github/workflows/legacy-node16-compat.yml (new, opt-in) - tools/actions/cache-normalize/action.yml (new composite action) - redwood-sdk-typescript/.github/workflows/ (removed duplicate CI) - redwood-sdk-python/.github/workflows/ (updated to reuse composite steps) - docs/ci.md (updated docs and runbook) - ci/scripts/cache-key.sh (added) Key implementation notes: - The unified workflow uses path filters and file-level heuristics to skip irrelevant jobs on docs-only or non-js changes. - Matrix pruning: we detect independent dimensions (os, node) and only expand when changes touch those areas. Defaults avoid an 18-node matrix explosion. - Cache normalization: we normalize npm and yarn lock hashing to improve cross-branch hits and add restore keys that fall back to prefix matches. - Release pipeline: unchanged release semantics; we kept the same tag and changelog logic, but artifacts are now produced in a single canonical job for easier debugging. Review conversation highlights: - Diego: asked for clearer failure visibility, requested job-level step summaries and direct links to failing logs. Addressed by adding a failure summary step that aggregates test failures for the most common test runners. - Priya: requested we avoid switching core SDKs to Node 20 until smoke tests pass. We added an opt-in matrix and left Python and Go pipelines untouched. - Samir: called out a flaky integration test that regressed due to increased parallelism; we introduced a concurrency-limited job for that specific test suite. CI run history: - Initial run (2025-11-13): cache-misses and one flaky integration failure; CI status: fail. Logs captured in comments. - Follow-up fixes (2025-11-14): added restore-keys and concurrency limits; rerun showed improvement. - Final e2e smoke-run (2025-11-19): all checks passed. CI summary: build: pass, lint: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, release-dry-run: pass. Performance: average workflow duration reduced from ~28m to ~17m on typical pushes with reduced matrix count; estimated GH Actions minute savings ~35% for active SDK repos. Rollout and migration notes: - This PR replaces and removes several legacy workflow files; maintainers should remove any local overrides that reintroduce duplicate workflows. - Repo-level secrets and required status checks remain unchanged; release automation still requires the release bot token. - A short runbook was added to docs/ci.md describing how to revert to legacy flows in emergencies. Linear and tracking: ENG-4821 tracked the initial consolidation work and ENG-4890 tracked cache/hits investigation. Merge decision: After two rounds of review and a clean safety smoke-run, this PR was squash-merged into main to keep history concise. Merge metadata: merged_at=2025-11-20, merge_method=squash, merged_by=Samir Patel. If regressions are observed: revert instructions are in docs/ci.md and the legacy-node16-compat workflow can be re-enabled immediately. Additional notes: - Kept the change backwards-compatible where possible. - No user-facing API changes. - Future work: evaluate GitHub self-hosted runner utilization and consider incremental job-level caching for large integration jobs.
